item.title: Introduction
item.description:
Introduction

NONMEM (Nonlinear Mixed Effects Model) is software for fitting nonlinear regression models to data. It is commonly used in pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic studies. In these studies, a drug is given to subjects and drug concentrations are measured over time, often in blood plasma. NONMEM uses a mixed-effects framework. It models variability between subjects (random effects). It also models variability within subjects and the influence of measured covariates (fixed effects). The models are nonlinear to reflect biochemical and physiological processes. NONMEM works well when each subject has only a few measurements. It also handles situations where sampling times differ between subjects. Although widely used in pharmaceutical applications, the underlying method is general. It can be applied to many nonlinear mixed-effects problems.
